outlier: Go 1.14 RC1, the state of Go in 2020, and ten Go development principles.

recent_posts.title: Golang Weekly Issue 599: May 1, 2026
recent_posts.summary: Golang Weekly Issue 599 covers a range of Go topics including zero-config heap profiling via runtime internals, a deep dive into Go's new Swiss table map implementation with benchmarks, and a comparison of Go logging libraries in 2026. Notable releases include Rapid 1.3 (property-based testing), Limen (composable authentication library), MongoDB Go Driver 2.6, Go-MySQL-Driver 1.10, rqlite 10.0, and Fiber 3.2. Also featured: building a userspace TCP-over-UDP stack in pure Go, a beginner guide to sync.Mutex, and GopherCon 2026 ticket availability.

recent_posts.title: Golang Weekly Issue 598: April 24, 2026
recent_posts.summary: Issue 598 of Golang Weekly covers several Go-focused articles: building a minimal container from scratch using Linux namespaces, a deep dive into the Go runtime's network poller (covering epoll/kqueue/IOCP and goroutine parking), a comparison of Go and Rust startup times, a production-grade Raft implementation designed to fail, and real-time goroutine tracing with eBPF.

recent_posts.title: Golang Weekly Issue 597: April 17, 2026
recent_posts.summary: Golang Weekly Issue 597 curates several Go-focused articles and tools: a deep dive into the Go compiler internals to implement a conditional expression syntax; watgo, a zero-dependency pure Go WebAssembly toolkit for parsing WAT and creating WASM binaries; a guide on error translation in layered Go services using domain sentinels; and gontainer, a reflection-based dependency injection container from NVIDIA with no external dependencies.

recent_posts.title: Golang Weekly Issue 596: April 10, 2026
recent_posts.summary: Golang Weekly issue 596 covers a range of Go ecosystem news. Highlights include Solod, a Go subset that compiles to C for systems programming without a runtime; constmap, an immutable Go map offering 3x faster lookups and 6x less memory at the cost of limited key types; Google's Agent Development Kit for Go reaching v1.0 with OpenTelemetry, self-healing logic, and safety guardrails; and several articles on Go patterns including multi-step sequences, the outbox pattern with Postgres, and a proposal for composite type constraints.

recent_posts.title: Golang Weekly Issue 595: March 27, 2026
recent_posts.summary: Golang Weekly issue 595 curates several Go-focused resources: a practical guide to Go naming conventions covering identifiers, filenames, and packages; a deep dive by a Go compiler engineer on type construction and cycle detection improvements in Go 1.26; and a roundup of ecosystem news including the origin story of Go's gopher mascot, a terminal music player built with Go and Bubble Tea, a survey of open source projects' stances on AI contributions, and an experimental Ruby-to-Go transpiler called Thanos.

recent_posts.title: Golang Weekly Issue 594: March 20, 2026
recent_posts.summary: Golang Weekly Issue 594 covers a gRPC-Go authorization bypass vulnerability urging upgrade to v1.79.3, a guide to Go profiling with pprof, an opinion on dependency cooldowns for Go, and a look at the GoTH stack with templUI. Notable releases include Hugo v0.158.0 with native CSS bundling, pq 1.12 Postgres driver, color 1.19.0, ncruces/go-sqlite3 0.32, argon2 1.5, and GoDoc Live for statically analyzing Go HTTP services to generate API docs.

recent_posts.title: Golang Weekly Issue 593: March 13, 2026
recent_posts.summary: Golang Weekly issue 593 curates Go ecosystem news including a benchmark of 15 string concatenation methods (favoring strings.Builder and strings.Join), a new declarative TUI library go-tui with React/Tailwind-inspired syntax, and articles on IEEE 754 decimal conversion, error wrapping patterns, and AI agents writing Go. Release highlights include Glamour 2.0, VHS 0.11, Testcontainers for Go 0.41, Mockery 3.7, and several other library updates.

recent_posts.title: Golang Weekly Issue 592: March 6, 2026
recent_posts.summary: Golang Weekly issue 592 covers Go 1.26.1 and 1.25.8 security releases fixing five vulnerabilities in crypto/x509, html/template, net/url, and os packages. Featured articles include a deep dive into stack allocation improvements in Go 1.25+ that reduce GC overhead, a guide on preventing silent mutex bugs using generic closures, and best practices for secure error handling. Also linked: opinions on why Go lacks a try keyword, Go for AI agents, and X.509 certificate verification vulnerabilities. Library releases include govips 2.17, eBPF 0.21, Gin 1.12, go-github 84.0, and several others.

recent_posts.title: Golang Weekly Issue 591: February 27, 2026
recent_posts.summary: Golang Weekly Issue 591 covers several notable Go ecosystem updates: the Charm TUI toolkit (Bubble Tea, Lip Gloss, Bubbles) has released synchronized v2 versions with a new faster renderer and improved APIs; Datadog shares how they reduced Go binary sizes by up to 77% using import graph pruning, dead code elimination, and linker tricks; Filippo Valsorda argues for replacing Dependabot with a better Go vulnerability scanner; new tools include witr (process inspector), gotreesitter (pure Go Tree-sitter runtime with 209 grammars), and finish (graceful HTTP server shutdowns).

recent_posts.title: Golang Weekly Issue 590: February 20, 2026
recent_posts.summary: Golang Weekly Issue 590 highlights Go 1.26's rewritten `go fix` tool, which automatically modernizes Go code using 24 built-in transformations such as replacing `interface{}` with `any` and adopting `strings.Cut`. The issue also covers `gog`, a CLI tool for accessing Google services (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, etc.) from the terminal, plus ecosystem notes including the Oat CSS/JS UI library, a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 overclocked to 873MHz running TinyGo, the Go2TV media casting app, and Bluebox Docker as a living Postgres sample database.
